decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work, the applicant shall submit, and have approved in writing by the local planning authority, a detailed layout, cross sections (scale 1:20), full specifications, and a detailed management and maintenance plan of the biodiverse roof with a minimum substrate depth of 80mm, not including the vegetative mat. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied. </p><p>REASON: In the interest of enhancing biodiversity, managing flood risk, and providing a sustainable drainage system.</p>

<p>Prior to occupation&nbsp;of the development hereby approved, details and full specifications of&nbsp;at least one bird or bat box&nbsp;shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, and shall be maintained for the lifespan of the development. The details should include:&nbsp;</p><p>A minimum of 1 bird box incorporated into the design of the development, with a variety of box types (including different sized entrance holes) to provide habitat for diverse bird species. </p><p>The boxes should be installed at or close to the eaves level of the development hereby approved. </p><p>The boxes should be between 3 and 5 metres from the ground, and there should be a clear flight path without any obstructions below and directly in front of the box. </p><p>The boxes should be facing north, east or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided), and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. </p><p>Boxes located in the same area should not be placed too close together.</p><p>REASON:&nbsp;To support bird and bat populations, including swifts, in Hackney and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing nesting opportunities, in accordance with Hackney’s Local Plan LP33 policy LP47 which states that all development schemes involving buildings with an eaves height or roof commencement height of 5 metres and above are required to provide nesting boxes for swifts, sparrows, starlings, and/or bats as appropriate</p>

All new external materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works to be carried out in this connection) shall match the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution, and finished appearance.


REASON: In the interests of the visual amenities of the surrounding area.
description: Single-storey ground floor rear extension and extension above two storey back addition, including levelling back garden.
